The Contractor is responsible for all aspects of civil engineering design. This shall include architectural, civil, structural and building services design for all temporary and permanent works. The civil works shall be designed to have a minimum working life of fifty (50) years before any significant repair or replacement of the main structural elements and secondary structural elements/cladding. This section identifies the Owner's minimum design requirements and parameters that are to be provided by the C ontractor.
The  Contractor  shall  provide  all  building  services  (electricity,  telephone,  computer,  water,  HVAC,  fire protection  etc.)  and  ensure  that  they  are  readily  accessible  for  maintenance  and  repair  and  adequate clearance is provided from main structural members and foundations.
The choice of external building materials shall be durable against sandstorm erosion, saline and corrosive environment.
Any pipe or underground cables crossings outside the plant boundary under Roads and Railroads shall be designed and constructed such that, proper access for maintenance of the damaged part can be possible during O&M period without disturbing the traffics under Roads and Railroads.

Backfill placed for embankments, non-supportive and unpaved areas shall be compacted to at least 75% relative density (ASTM D 4253 and ASTM D 4254) for free draining soils containing less than 15% by weight finer than 75 micron sieve non plastic material or 90% of the maximum density as determined by ASTM D 1557for soils containing more than 15% material passing the 75 micron sieve.
Backfill placed below all the supports, roads and paved areas shall be minimum compacted to 85% relative density (ASTM D 4253 and ASTM D 4254) for free draining soils containing less than 15% by weight finer than 75 micron sieve non plastic material or 95% of the maximum density as determined by ASTM D 1557 for soils containing more than 15% material passing the 75 micron sieve.
A cap layer shall be placed to provide wind erosion protection in all the outdoor exposed areas. The cap layer shall be a minimum of 150 mm thick. The contractor to use soil-cement asphalt paving or sprayed-on polymer-based erosion inhibitors on that capping layer. Gravel layer is acceptable, as long as no erosion possibility is there due to water and wind. Gravel layer thickness 100 mm can be considered. However, this is subject to the Geotechnical recommendation.
For the design purpose, Design Ground water level shall be considered as per Geotechnical information, however  seasonal  variation  of  groundwater  and  capillary  rise  of  groundwater  shall  be  taken  into  the consideration for design and construction work and shall be substantiated before the start of design and construction work.
No foundations shall be supported on backfilled soil. Only less important and lighter foundation can be rested on backfilled soil subject to detail engineering and Owner's approval fulfilling the settlement requirement.
A  geotextile  layer  shall  be  put  between  the  filling  layer  and  the  soil  after  removal  of  top  layer  if recommended by EPC Geotechnical study.

Chunk Text:
Selected fill shall have the following properties:
Well graded having uniformity index of not less than 5. Selected fill shall be non-cohesive, free of plastic clays and having silt content not greater than 5%, salt content less than 3% and organic matter not greater than 2%. Decomposing or compressible materials shall not be acceptable.
The material shall be of such nature and character that it can be compacted to the specified densities. It shall be free of all materials subject to decay, decomposition or dissolution, and of cinders or other material that will corrode piping or other material.
The intention is to use selected fill below structures, below pipelines, backfill to structures, roads, parking areas and hard standings etc.

Search Query: Erosion Protection Works, soil-cement stabilization, compaction 98% maximum dry density, within 1% optimum moisture, ASTM D-558, Type V Portland Cement ASTM C 150, erosion control blankets, fibre rolls, coir logs, Tensar geo-grids, gravel layer 100 mm

Chunk Text:
If the surface soils is susceptible to wind and water erosion these shall be stabilized with Cement. The soil and cement should be well mixed, moisture conditioned to within 1 per cent of optimum moisture and compacted to at least 98% of the maximum dry density. The optimum moisture content and maximum dry density of the soil-cement mixture should be determined by the ASTM D-558 test method. Traffic, except as required to maintain the surface of the soil cement in a damp condition, should not be permitted for at least 24 hours after final compaction.
For slope protection against erosion from wind, stabilization of surface soil with Type V Portland Cement as per ASTM C 150 may be adopted. For slope protection against erosion from water, slowing down of surface water is needed. To accomplish this, erosion control blankets, fibre rolls may be used. Erosion control blankets are usually woven type from a chosen material, with lots of ridges and obstructions. These materials are either synthetic or natural. Fibber rolls are also made of similar material as used in erosion control blankets but are rolled into large diameter logs. Coir type logs/ Logs made of rice/wheat straw also may be used. These logs are nailed into the slope to slow down the surface water. Tensar type geo-grids also may be effective. The source/ availability of the appropriate material is essential in selection of the technique, and it shall be duly approved by the Owner's engineer.
Gravel layer is acceptable, as long as no erosion possibility is there due to water and wind. Gravel layer thickness 100 mm can be considered.

The safe working capacity of the pile(s) shall be determined by calculation using recognized soil mechanic principles and equations. The Contractor shall carry out a programme of preliminary test piling at site to verify his designs prior to commencing the installation of permanent 'working' piles. The maximum load applied during the preliminary pile testing programme shall be 200% of pile working load. The settlement limit in this case shall follow relevant applicable International/local standards. Upon completion of testing preliminary piles shall be cut down and abandoned, such piles may not be incorporated into the permanent works construction.
For the structural design of the piles the recommendations in ACI 318M-08/318RM08: 'Metric Building Code Requirements for Structural Concrete and Commentary' and ACI 543R -00 Design, Manufacture and Installation of Concrete Piles and the requirements of this OTS shall be followed.
Permissible pile settlements at under load for compression, tension and lateral load tests shall not exceed settlement criteria imposed by plant manufacturers, local regulations or shall conform with the BS 8004, whichever is the most stringent. With ys, sls >= 1.0, the settlement of an individual pile shall be limited to less than 3% of its diameter, D; with 1.2, the settlement shall he limited to less than 1.5% D complying BS 8004 requirements.
If piles are required to resist dynamic loads they shall not be loaded to more than 50% and 85% of their safe working load during normal (dead, live and other sustain load) and abnormal operating conditions (wind, seismic and other transient load) respectively.
The design of the foundations for plant subject to dynamic loads shall be in accordance with DIN 4024 : Part 1 (1988) 'Machine Foundations' and CP 2012 : Part 1 'Foundations for Reciprocating Machines'. If manufacturer's design guide is not coincided with above mentioned code, then manufacturer's guide shall be considered preferentially
The bearing pressure under foundations subject to dynamic loads shall not exceed 60% and 90% of the safe ground bearing pressure during normal and abnormal operating conditions respectively.
The  overall  and  differential  settlement  of  foundations  for  plant  shall  strictly  adhere  to  the  plant manufacturer's requirements or accepted standards which is more stringent.
The allowable overall settlement for the isolated foundations shall not exceed 25 mm. The allowable overall settlement for the raft foundations shall not exceed 50 mm. The allowable differential settlement for the tanks  ring  beam  foundations  shall  be  designed  in  accordance  with  API  650.  The  allowable  overall settlement after the hydrotest for the tank foundations supported on ring beams shall not be more than 50mm.

The Steam turbine buildings shall provide protection of the equipment, electrical enclosed installation and controls from the environmental conditions. The buildings shall be designed for noise attenuation and be of non-combustible construction. The buildings shall be dust proof type and ventilated so that the building internal Design Temperature should not be greater than 5°C above maximum ambient temperature. The entrances shall be sufficiently sized to provide access for the largest item to be located within respective Building.
The  building  shall  be  of  sufficient  size  to  facilitate  the  installation  operation  and  maintenance  of  all components and equipment housed therein.  Requisite lay-down areas shall be provided for O&M purpose. Entrances shall be suitably sized and located to facilitate maintenance requirements.
Proper handling arrangement shall be provided for the equipment for O&M period.
Sufficient  capacities  of  cranes  shall  be  erected  for  normal  maintenance  of  the  gas  turbine  auxiliaries, including lifting heavy parts such as the casing and rotor.
Suitable access to the turbine building shall be provided to allow access for single complete rotors. A rotor unstacking area shall be provided with a suitable foundation to enable unstacking of a single rotor in the upright position and all necessary equipment shall be provided to manoeuvre and support the rotor. The turbine laydown/maintenance area may also function as the rotor unstacking area; however the Contractor shall take due care of the space usage and functionality.
Suitable  paved  areas  outside  the  Turbine  Buildings  to  put  the  mobile  crane  and  a  low  bed  trailer,  for transportation of the disassembled parts, in a stable way.
The separate turbine enclosures will be foreseen with easily removable panel(s) that can be lifted by the crane and can be put aside and foresee walkways with railings, sufficient lighting, around the roof and around the roof opening(s) that, with a connection in between the walkways.
The separate turbine enclosure shall be foreseen with removable  beams to connect hoists in strategic locations, such as above the combustion chambers.
The floor slab within the building, which incorporates pipe and cable trenches shall be constructed of reinforced concrete laid flat and with local dishing incorporated adjacent to floor gully inlets. Floor drains shall discharge via a piped drainage network into oily water separators. Trench covers shall be designed to accept the appropriate floor loading according to their location and shall be manually removable.
Emergency exits fitted with panic escape bars shall be provided to all areas of the turbine buildings and annexes and boiler enclosures. Steel doors and frames should comply with the fire rating requirements. These openings must be kept clear of all obstructions.

The GT and ST foundations shall be a monolithic raft supported by piles  if required as per the Geotechnical report.  The  exhaust  stack  may  be  supported  by  a  separate  foundation  or  incorporated  within  the foundation if required by the Contractor.
The contractor shall ensure that the following points are included in the GT and ST foundation works:
- a. A minimum rebar content of 80 kg/m 3  of concrete shall be provided.
- b. The design of the GT and ST foundation shall satisfy, in addition to an appropriate internationally recognized design code on machine foundations, the following codes: ACI 351,  CP 2012 and DIN 4024. CP 2012  requires an  internal  reinforcement cage system which is essential for the foundation to act as a homogenous mass and provide a second line of defence to the machine anchoring system with the holding down bolts. DIN 4024 provides guidelines for carrying out dynamic analysis.

- c. The GT and ST foundation shall be isolated from the rest of the works by floor joints.
- d. The ratio of mass of the foundation to mass of the GT and ST plant shall be at least 2.
- e. To reduce the risk of dynamic compaction the maximum load on any pile supporting a GT and ST foundation shall not exceed 60 per cent of its working capacity during the normal operating conditions and shall not exceed 90 per cent in extreme conditions. For a foundation supported by soil the same limits apply to the allowable bearing capacity of the soil.
- f. The design  of  the  GT  and  ST  foundations  shall  include  the  thermal  effects  on  the foundation and its ability to withstand the extreme differential temperatures likely to be experienced by the foundation, during the construction as well as throughout its design life. Protective measures during construction shall be part of the design.
- g. The section  of  the  GT  and  ST  foundation  below  ground  shall  be  protected  with  a coating system to resist attack from the sulphate content in the soils and chlorides from the ground water. Further protection against corrosion of the reinforcement (which leads to expansion of the concrete and cracking) due to the severe chloride ion content of the soils and groundwater shall be provided as covered by the concrete section of this Specification.
- h. The GT and ST foundation shall be poured in one operation and construction joints are not permitted unless in exceptional circumstances and with the approval of the Owner/Owner's Engineer.
- i. The design, detailing and construction of the GT and ST foundations shall allow fully for  the  'buildability'  of  the  foundations,  particularly  where  congested  areas  of reinforcement are required.
- j. In addition to the static structural design the contractor shall prove the design of the turbine  supporting  structure  dynamically  by  modelling  the  bearing  points,  the foundation and the soil body together, taking the full consideration of the coupling effect and interaction between the three systems.
- k. The  design  of  turbine  supporting  structures,  if  applicable,  shall  be  same  as  that supporting the gas turbines except in some designs a table top structure and columns are erected over a mat foundation. The supporting structure if cast monolithically shall  be  analysed  with  due  consideration  of  the  flexibility  of  each  structural component.  If the table top structure is supported by springs the substructure may be  designed  as  a  static  structure  if  its  superstructure  proves  a  sufficient  isolation achieved by the springs.
The Contractor shall submit thermal curing procedures for the steam turbine and gas turbine foundations to the Owner/Owner's Engineer for approval prior to commencing construction of these works.

The Contractor shall pay especial attention for the unknown amount of cavities, voids and interconnecting discontinuities  and  shall  ensure  that  the  locations  of  all  significant  plant  and  building  foundations  are thoroughly probed for voids and discontinuities as part of his supplementary ground investigation studies.
To mitigating the settlement risk the cavities and voids may be grouted injected if they are found below the major foundations. Alternately the foundations may be founded on piles.
The design of piled foundations for major structures and buildings shall conform to the settlement criteria stated earlier of the specification.
Following activities are mandatory for the Foundation design and construction:
- The depth of the Borehole shall be considered based on following criteria as a minimum: British  Standard:  Code  of  practice  for  site  investigations  BS  5930:1999  Section '12.7.2 Foundations for structures
- Geophysical tests at the key foundations (to be agreed with Owner) locations to be carried out before the construction/erection of foundations
- If cavities are found, required soil improvement/ foundation design criteria to be carried out subject to OE approval.
- Dewatering methodology will have to be demonstrated is fit for purpose according to soil conditions and submitted for Owner approval. Particular attention to be paid to those soils that can be degraded and/or settled due to dewatering process.
- Dewatering  shall  ensure  to  restrict  the  movement  of  fine  grain  material  below  the foundation level.
- The  dewatering  work  shall  be  performed  with  reputed  local  Specialize  contractor.  The
- Contractor for dewatering and the Dewatering process shall be approved by the Owner. Dewatering design shall be submitted for owner's approval. Following criteria shall be given special consideration while designing the foundation:
- Effect of surrounding foundations shall be considered when pressure bulbs supposed to be overlapping. For key foundations raft foundations will be prefer design criteria.

Chunk Text:
Design and construction standards and criteria for roads shall be in accordance with the local regulations and AASHTO requirements.
The final road network design shall incorporate two major considerations:
- Full  accessibility  to  the  offshore  facilities  and  on-shore  plant  ensuring  that  all  operational  and maintenance requirements can be fulfilled in an efficient manner including interfaces with the existing road network;
- Security, protection and safety of the employees and the Plant
A road system shall be provided to serve all buildings on the Site.
The roads shall be constructed between raised kerbs and graded to falls leading surface water into gullies or catch pits that will connect into the surface water drainage system. Gullies shall be provided with grating to prevent the ingress of debris into the drains.
Road pavements are to be designed to for a 25 years design period.
The roads shall be constructed in reinforced concrete or in flexible bituminous concrete (asphalt minimum of two layers) construction, depending upon the location. Concrete roads shall be used in areas of heavy and  abnormal  loading,  where  oil  spillage  may  occur  and  where  a  durable  and  maintenance  free construction  is  essential  to  the  movement  of  plant  and  equipment.  All  other  roads  shall  be  of  flexible construction with a bituminous concrete (asphalt) finish.
Sidewalk shall be provided for all the roads where it is necessary to satisfy person's walking requirement.
.
Main and Secondary Access Gate and Main and Minor Gate house shall be considered for entry/exit the plant.

Internal fences for the safety of any particular installation within the Plant Site shall be erected completely with all necessary doors and gates. The American standards may be used in addition to the local code.
Each type of internal fencing shall suit the level of security required by each installation. In general, each level of security shall be agreed with the Owner, however a 3 level master key security system shall be provided as a minimum.
Straining posts shall be provided at all ends and corners, at changes in direction or acute variations in level and at intervals of not more than 60m in straight lengths of fence. Struts shall be fitted to all straining posts, in the direction of each line of fencing. Steel struts and posts shall be bolted together. Intermediate posts shall be provided at intervals, measured centre-to-centre, of not more than 3m.
All building doors, equipment room or container doors and fence gate lock keys shall be operable by Grand Master key and to the approval of the Owner.
As per NFPA regulations, transformer shall be enclosed by fire walls. The entrance side shall be provided with a removable security internal fence fitted with a lockable personnel access gate compatible with Master key system.
The plant Area and sub-station area shall been closed by fence or  wall meeting the national and local guidelines. The plant fence or walls shall be maintained throughout the construction phase and at no time security of any of the plant sites shall be compromised. The fencing shall be HCIS Category -1.
The design of the fences, gates , boundary walls and all other security installations shall follow the local requirements. Internal fences for the safety of any particular installation within the Plant Site shall be erected completely with all necessary doors and gates. The American standards may be used in addition to the local code.
Internal fencing shall suit the level of security required by each installation. In general each level of security shall  be  agreed  with  the  Owner,  however  a  3  level  master  key  security  system  shall  be  provided  as  a minimum.
Mechanized Vehicular gates shall be double opening. Gates shall be furnished with hinges of a type which prevent the easy removal of gates from the gate posts. Gate hinges shall allow the gate to swing through 180°.  The  gates  shall  use  the  same  type  of  wire  mesh  as  used  for  the  fencing.  Emergency  opening mechanical push bars shall be provided to all personnel gates. Locking bars shall be provided to all vehicle gates and provision made for the attachment of a padlock which shall be accessible from both sides of the gate.
Hazards areas like transformer, fuel areas shall be protected with the internal fence and gate.
All building doors, equipment room or container doors and fence gate lock keys shall be operable by Grand Master key and to the approval of the Owner.
Sand preventing arrangement/sand fence shall be provided as required for the smooth operation of the plant to prevent the ingress of sand. The structural design of the fence shall consider loads if any from the deposited sand.

All buildings in the Plant shall be paved with minimum 150 mm concrete extending from the edge of the building  for  a  distance  of  1.2m  with  proper  slope  to  drainage  Surface  Water  Drainage  System  and additionally asphalted paving shall be extending from 1.2 m up to a distance of 5.0m with proper slope to drainage Surface Water Drainage System if the soil is erosion prone due to water and wind.
A surface water drainage system shall be provided for the Plant. The design shall allow for the separate collection, treatment and disposal of surface water over the whole of the Site (arising from run-off of natural water from buildings, roads, ground surface, paved areas, etc.). All buildings shall be provided with roof drainage for disposal of surface water, and be connected to the surface water drainage system. The surface water drainage system shall be arranged and designed to effectively manage all run-off and discharge arising from the Site.
The Storm  water  Drainage  system  shall  be  designed  considering  100  years  rainfall  return  period  and rainfall intensity equal to the retention period.
Basements, cable and pipe trenches and tunnels shall be constructed with adequate provision for drainage. Floors to basements, trenches and tunnels shall be laid to falls and/or drainage channels provided therein. Any water entering the basements trenches or tunnels shall be routed to sumps and connected to the surface water drainage system. Where connection to the surface water drainage system is not practical, then provision to pump-out water from the trench or tunnel drainage sump, by permanent and/or portable sump pumps shall be made. Fire deluge water shall be gathered into storm water catch pits and discharged via main storm water system and prevented from entering tunnels.
Primary site drainage and sub-soil drainage shall be provided, where necessary, on external areas generally to protect the site from run off into building areas etc.
Storm water drainage sumps, pumps and electrical equipment shall be located to avoid hazardous areas. If unavoidable then the pumps and electrical equipment shall conform to the requirements in accordance with API and NFPA for operation in hazardous environments. Pumps shall be able to be withdrawn from the sump at surface level for maintenance and repair. The sump and valve chamber shall be equipped with access covers and ladders for maintenance purposes. The sump chamber shall be designed hydraulically so as not to impair pump performance.
Additionally,  ESIA  requirement  shall  be  completely  followed  for  storm  water  design  including  for  the requirement of Storm water basin.

The  Contractor  shall  be  responsible  for  design  of  wastewater  drainage  system  complying  with  the Environmental Regulations and other applicable regulations with respect to wastewater. The Contractor shall provide the following to comply with local environmental protection requirements.
The Plant shall be designed with Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) which means that no emissions of liquid effluents  other  than  uncontaminated  storm  water  will  be  discharged  to  the  environment.  Hence,  all wastewaters will be directed to an evaporation pond  where the accumulating sludge will regularly be disposed.
The Contractor shall present a concept for the wastewater treatment plants and demonstrate the major waste water treatment steps including the corresponding maximum and normal flows.
Treated waste waters from operations that are known to produce effluents will be directed to a dedicated sump  where  they  can  be  neutralised  before  being  pumped  to  an  evaporation  pond.  Transformer compounds: provide storage contamination and separation facilities for oil spillage;
- Main building plant drainage: oil spillage, effluent from HRSG cleaning, HRSG blowdown, air heater wash  and  other  non-oily  contaminated  sources,  provide  oil  separators,  chemical  treatment  and sedimentation facilities/evaporation pond.
The treated effluent shall be discharged by pumping or gravity, ultimately to the final discharge point.
Effluent discharged from station processes shall be treated to comply with local environmental protection requirements. Effluent discharged from station processes into the chemical drains, dirty drains and clean drains shall be routed directly, after treatment, to the final discharge point.

Chunk Text:
A sanitary wastewater and sewage drainage system shall be provided to allow for the separate collection, treatment and disposal of foul water (arising from toilets, urinals, sinks, etc.).
The sanitary wastewater and sewage drainage system shall be laid in straight lines between manholes. The systems  shall  be  self-cleansing  and  function  with  the  minimum  of  maintenance,  and  access  shall  be provided so that it is possible to rod the whole of the drainage system. The effluent shall be directed to a self-contained package type sewage treatment plant. The quality of all temporary and permanent drainage discharges from the Site shall comply with the local authority requirements.
Sanitary  wastewater  shall,  to  the  extent  possible,  be  plant  internally  re-used  after  its  treatment  for irrigation purposes. Its sludge shall be used, if applicable, as fertilizer.
For this reuse, the PME's/NCEC's General Environmental Regulations and Rules for Implementation apply. The sewage system shall consist of a piping system with inspection manholes every  60 m and at each change of direction
The piping  and  collection  system  shall  provide  holding  capacity  adequate  for  a  72  hour  failure  of  the treatment system without overflow.

Providing  of  any  underground  storage  tank  of  any  size  designed  to  contain  petroleum  products  or Hazardous Substances should be avoided. If underground installations is deemed necessary, all such tanks shall:
- Be provided in an impervious liners or structures (e.g. concrete vault) under or around tanks and lines that direct any leaked product to monitoring ports at the lowest point of the liner or structure or constructed with double walls; and
- Be provisioned with gauges to measure the material volume inside the tank for reconciling tank content, leak detection, automatic fill shutoff valves and level overflow alarms that are transmitted to a continuously attended workstation (e.g. from the Control room).
Impervious  liners  or  structures  shall  be  fabricated  of  material  appropriate  for  the  substance  being contained in the underground storage tanks. If a double walled tank is provided, means shall be provided to detect leaks between the walls.
Contractor shall report to the Owner why an underground tank is proposed and how its design meets Owner's minimum requirements for underground tank installation and operation.

All areas used to unload/load transportation vehicles (e.g. tank, trucks) of liquid hazardous substances or petroleum products shall be provisioned with impervious secondary spill containment provisioned with a means to drain accumulated rain water  in  a  controlled  fashion  (i.e.  using  a  lockable  drain  valve).  The capacity of the impervious spill containment system must be capable of containing one hundred ten percent (110%) of the largest spill (e.g., truck capacity) and a free board of 250mm. Check valve and leak-proof piping connections shall be used for the transfer pipe system to prevent a release in the event of a system failure.
Back-up Fuel oil tanks shall be placed on reinforced concrete ring foundations and be located inside a oil and water tight tank basin of reinforced concrete slabs and surrounding walls with respective oil proof coating.

- The stiffness value has to be ascertained carefully depending on the route and overburden loading.
- Heavy Vehicle routes to be marked clearly with labels and signage.
- A specialized independent third party shall be appointed by the Contractor with the approval of the Owner for design review and Supervision of in-situ installation and testing.
- Following requirement shall be considered as mandatory.
- The specialized independent third party to review and approve the type of joints for the FRP pipe.
- The specialized independent third party to supervise of laying of FRP onshore pipeline.
- The specialized independent third party to review and approve the design for FRP pipeline installation and  backfilling,  MoS  for  the  laying  of  FRP  pipeline  including  the  backfilling  and  bedding  material quality, FRP Pipe trench sizing and type of FRP pipe joints.

- The specialized independent third party shall be subject to the approval of the Owner
- Proper marking on roadways for the movement of heavy equipment on FRP pipeline routing.
- Where applicable, thrust blocks, which are concrete pipe thrust restraints or anchors placed up against underground pipe fittings, should be used to prevent movement of underground pipes from thrust forces in water mains.
- Also, and where applicable, permanent markers for underground utilities like cable duct banks, direct buried cables, pipes etc. shall be specified.
- When encasing FRP lines in concrete, we should use a Neoprene pad to protect the pipe, or if the pipe crosses a road, we could install it within a trench or sleeve, which is a good solution because there will be no weight transfer to the pipe. The bottom line is that the concrete must not come into direct contact with the FRP pipe.
- In addition to the above requirements, the Document Management system for the Fibre Glass Pipeline, shall  be  included  as  Schedule  R  of  this  Specification  and  shall  be  followed  by  the  Contractor. Chunk Text:
All buildings shall be designed to ensure that internal noise, vibration, temperature and dust levels are kept within acceptable limits to provide proper operating conditions for the plant which is to be installed and a comfortable working environment for the Owner's operations and maintenance staff throughout the year. Noise limitations have been specified around the turbine housings and the design and construction shall fully take this into account.
Roofs -typically flat roofs with single ply solar reflective waterproofing membrane (with protection) over rigid  insulation  over  concrete slabs, however  the material and construction are the Companies design. However, maximum U-value shall of 0.19 W/m2K shall apply to habitable or air-conditioned buildings. The above requirements or local requirement and standards which one is stringent shall be followed.
Walls -concrete structures with concrete masonry units as infill with insulation and a decorative render finish however the material and construction are the Companies design. However, maximum U-value shall of  0.2  W/m2K  shall  apply  to  habitable  or  air-conditioned  buildings.  The  above  requirements  or  local requirement and standards which one is stringent shall be followed.
Rock wool (Type A) insulation shall be used for the insulated cladding.
The Contractor shall make provision in the designs for the maintenance of all high-level buildings, both internally and externally.
The architectural concept for the Plant buildings, including colour schemes and finishes schedules, shall be finalized and agreed with the Owner/Owner's Engineer at an early stage in the design process.
The dimensions of buildings shall provide adequate space for the safe installation and operation of all plant and equipment, its replacement, and for maintenance procedures.

The loads identified below shall be considered in design; where relevant, the appropriate codes and basic design parameters are also given.
- Dead -All  dead  loading  shall  be  in  accordance  with  ANSI/ASCE 7-16 'Minimum Design  Loads  for Buildings and Other Structures ' and more specifically BS 648.  The self-weight of structure, floors, roofing, side cladding and internal partition walls shall be treated as dead loads. Fixed plant loadings shall be treated as dead loads.
- Live -Live loading shall be in accordance with ANSI/ASCE 7-22 'Minimum Design Loads for Buildings and Other Structures'. The Contractor shall determine the correct superimposed loading for all floor areas  based on design criteria. ASCE 7-22, IBC 2024 and supplier's input details.
In addition to all plant loadings, the minimum live loads to be considered in the HRSG structure, turbine housings and annexes shall not be less than:
- Turbine House suspended concrete floors live load 10 kN/m 2
- Firing aisles on burner Platforms in the boiler structure 7.5 kN/m 2
- Turbine House open grid floors live load 7.5 kN/m 2
- Auxiliary cable floors live load 7.5 kN/m 2
- Switchgear and control room floors live load 7.5 kN/m 2

The Contractor shall grub up and remove vegetation of any kind which is established on the site of the new works. The removal and reinstallation of the existing facilities shall be within EPC Contractor's scope. The modification and adjustment of the existing facilities if required shall be within the scope of the Contractor.
The modification, removal, reinstallation work shall be carried out as per Owner and Offtaker approval.
The Contractor shall carry out excavation in any type of soil found. Stripping off of topsoil as required shall be  carried  out  for  both  the  plant  areas.  Any  obstructions  encountered  in  the  excavations  such  as  old foundations, abandoned drainage systems, etc. shall be broken out and removed in their entirety. Any excavations so formed shall be filled with well compacted granular fill to the approval of the Owner.
The gradation of granular fill materials used in the works shall produce a stable compacted fill.
Satisfactory soils shall be identified by the Contractor, from his geotechnical investigations and written recommendations. Satisfactory soils shall be capable of being compacted to meet the requirements of the Specification  whilst  also  fulfilling  the  requirements  of  the  Contractors  detailed  design  of  the  works, including loading and safe bearing pressure, settlement, stability, drainage, buildability, etc. They include ASTM D 2487 and ASTM D 3282 Soil Classification Groups: GW, GP, GM, SW, SP, and SM, or a combination of these groups; AASHTO M 145 Soil Classification Groups A-1, Plasticity Index less than 6, free of rock or gravel larger than 75 mm in any dimension, debris, waste, vegetation, and other deleterious matter.  In addition, the satisfactory soils will be applied to the structural area such as equipment foundation and buildings and may not be applied to other non-structural areas.
Unsatisfactory soils shall be identified by the Contractor from his geotechnical investigations and written recommendations. They include ASTM D 2487 Soil Classification Groups: GC, SC, ML, MH, CL, CH, OL, OH, and PT, or a combination of these groups. Also, AASHTO M 145 Soil Classification Groups A-2-6, A-2-7, A-4, A-5, A-6, and A-7. The Contractor shall notify the Owner/Owner's Engineer regarding the discovery and extent  of  any  unsatisfactory  material  with  recommendations  for  remediation.  Unsatisfactory  materials shall not be mixed or stockpiled with satisfactory materials.

To  achieve  the  service  life  specified,  a  high  quality,  durable  concrete  shall  be  provided  to  protect reinforcement, embedded metals and concrete against attack from aggressive chemicals such as chlorides, sulphates and other agents.
The Contractor shall take the following key exposure categories into account whilst preparing the design mix(s) requirements. Design mix(s) shall be subject to the Owner's/Owner's Engineer's approval.
- Concrete below ground level.
- Internal concrete.
All structural concrete shall develop a minimum compressive cylinder strength (f'c) of 35 N/mm 2  at 28 days. (This shall be equivalent to a cube strength of 42 N/mm 2 ). However, for the superstructure located in  ambient  conditions,    cylindrical  strength  of  31  N/mm2  at  28  days  will  be  acceptable  if  proven  for required durability and Local regulations.
Blinding concrete shall have a minimum thickness of 75mm and minimum 28 day cube strength of 20.0 N/mm 2 . Also, the blinding concrete in contact with Sea water shall have a minimum 28 day cube strength of 20.0 N/mm 2,  unless more stringent strength requirement is there as per local regulations. Non-structural mass filling concrete can be considered to have a minimum 28 day cube strength 15 N/mm2. The minimum thickness of lean concrete shall be 75mm.
In the event that slip formed construction is offered for any part of the works then a special concrete design shall be developed by the Contractor and offered to the Owner/Owner's Engineer for approval.
The outer surface of the concrete in contact with ground and ground water has to be protected with a waterproof bituminous membrane. Minimum one additional corrosion protection method such as use of corrosion inhibitor, cathodic protection or coated reinforcement.
For all reinforced concrete, the recommendation for Geotechnical Investigation report and CIRIA guidelines shall be followed.

Admixtures shall  be  selected  by  the  Contractor  to  accommodate  his  requirements  for  placing  of  fresh concrete.
The Contractor shall demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Owner/Owner's Engineer that the intended durability  of  the  concrete  mix  for  the  required  design  life  can  be  satisfied  for  the  particular  exposure environment.
The Contractor shall ensure that the Concrete is not adversely affected by the climate factors, namely, higher air temperature, low relative humidity and wind velocity. Air and concrete thermometers shall be kept  on  the  site.  Concrete  shall  not  be  placed  if  the  shade  temperature  exceeds  40ºC  or  the  concrete temperature exceeds 30ºC. Temperature thermocouples shall be placed in the mass concrete foundations to monitor the heat of hydration for concrete. The differential temperature between core and surface shall not be more than 20°C.
The Contractor shall be responsible for ensuring that all constituent materials used for the concrete works (e.g. cementitous, aggregate, reinforcement, water, admixtures etc) comply with recognized international material standards and methods of testing and meet the requirements of this Specification. The use of proposed constituent materials shall be agreed with the Owner/Owner's Engineer prior to their use on the Project.
The following values of minimum reinforcement cover shall be provided:
For all external works at faces cast in contact with the ground water, capillary zone of groundwater or seawater (Onshore), 25/50mm = 75mm. Reinforcement in slabs, columns and beams (onshore) - exposed to ambient weather - exposed to ground and not in contact with groundwater, 25/50mm = 50mm 75mm. Reinforcement in slabs, columns and beams (offshore): - not permanently/intermittently submerged in sea water or exposed to sea water splashing, - permanently/intermittently submerged in sea water or exposed to sea water splashing, 25/50mm = 75 mmoras per applicable code 75 mmoras per applicable code
Cover for the concrete in contact with seawater and splash zone shall follow the relevant codes.
In addition, the Contractor shall provide sufficient concrete cover and overall cross-sectional dimensions to ensure the correct fire protection to the various elements of structure (where fire protection is required) are  achieved.  This  shall  be  in  accordance  with  ACI-216  1-97/TMS  0216.1-97  "Standard  Method  of determining Fire Resistance of Concrete and Masonry Construction Assemblies.
For below ground concrete protective measures shall, as a minimum be provided to meet the requirements of  and  as  specified  below.  The  contractor  shall  assess  sulphate,  chloride  and  pH  levels  existing  in representative soil and groundwater samples as part of his programme of supplementary geotechnical investigation  of  the  site.  The  concrete  protective  measures  set  out  below  shall  be  upgraded  where necessary based on these.

Parts of the structure within the capillary rise zone or below ground water table, Sulphate levels below 6.0 g/l (groundwater) 6.7 g/l (soil). = Bitumen emulsion paint and minimum cover to reinforcement shall be as per ACI standard and local regulations.. Parts of the structure within the capillary rise zone or below ground water table, Sulphate levels in excess of 6.0 g/l (groundwater) 6.7 g/l (soil). = Bitumen emulsion paint and minimum cover to reinforcement shall be as per ACI standard and local regulations.. Precast concrete piles, Sulphate levels below 6.0 g/l (groundwater) 6.7 g/l (soil). = Steel moulds.. Precast concrete piles, Sulphate levels in excess of 6.0 g/l (groundwater) 6.7 g/l (soil). = Steel moulds
Note that the depth of the capillary rise zone shall be taken as 1.5 m above the highest ground water level (considering seasonal variation) for underground facility design and construction. Sulphate and chloride levels shall be determined by the Contractor's soil investigation.
Bitumastic paint shall be applied on top of all blinding concrete if recommended by Geotech report except where horizontal shear resistance is required.
Embedded  materials  shall  be  accurately  fabricated  and  assembled  to  suit  the  construction  interface required.
All steel embedment in concrete shall be accurately positioned and securely anchored either directly to the formwork or by templates prior to pouring the concrete. Pockets for later insertion of assemblies generally will be allowed.
Embedment shall be clean both before they are installed and after placement of the concrete.
Where embedment are required for major equipment items e.g. Turbine Generator, Pump Foundations, etc, then anchor bolts, attachments and embedment shall be located and secured prior to concrete placement with accurately made steel templates. In the above cases tolerances shall be as specified by the equipment manufacturer . Templates shall be interconnected and braced with steel members that maintain the anchor bolt alignment and position.
However, penetrating type of bolts are accepted if recommended by OEM.
Welding of embedment, to the reinforcement cage to secure their location, will not be accepted.
Corrosion protection shall be provided to all embedment, suitable to the environment in which they are cast. Generally, the following exposure conditions shall be considered as a minimum:
- Dry internal environments;
- Wet internal environments;
- External environments not exposed to seawater or seawater spray;
- External environments exposed to seawater spray/splash zone;

The materials that will be used for embedded items shall of stainless steel or carbon steel (e.g. sub-plate) as per proven experience and aggressiveness of the environment. The selection of material will be based on strength and durability requirements. Additionally, the choice of material may be dictated by interfacing issues with plant requirements.
The  necessity  of  welding  plant  fixings  etc.  to  embedment  exposed  at  the  concrete  surface  in  exposed environments shall be considered at design stage and wherever possible alternative fixing details shall be provided in order to preserve the original corrosion protective coatings.
Where this detail cannot be designed out then to protect the embedded item(s) from corrosion, for the life of the station, the following minimum material requirements and corrosion protection criteria shall be provided.
- All anchor bolts shall have a concrete cover of at least 100 mm.
The  corrosion  protection  system  provided  to  concrete  embedment  shall  also  consider  the  corrosion protection system(s) provided to adjacent plant and the dual requirements shall be considered collectively, where applicable, to select the most appropriate solution.
Concrete construction tolerances shall comply with ACI 117.
The minimum lateral distance between adjacent individual spread footings bearing at the same grade on soil shall be B/2, where B is the footing width or diameter of the larger footing. For Square or rectangular footings, of width B, the minimum lateral separation distance should be no less than B.  Where the lateral spacing  is  less  than  recommended,  the  stress  distribution  between  the  adjacent  footings  should  be analysed.
Net design bearing capacities and settlement estimates for tanks shall be based on the assumption that the foundation soils underlying the tank are not significantly affected by adjacent tanks. The lateral distance between adjacent tanks should be limited to a distance B, where B is the diameter of the smaller of two adjacent tanks. If the tanks are spaced at a distance less than B, the differential settlement between the centre and edge could be about 15 percent larger.
Furthermore, the landscaping shall be at least 3 m away from the proposed structure perimeters. A 1.2-m wide concrete or asphalt apron could be constructed adjacent to buildings around the perimeters to protect the foundation soils from surface water and sloped away from the structures to facilitate drainage. Water lines should, if possible, be kept away from the foundations.  In addition, consideration should be given to the use of an impermeable membrane placed around building perimeters to a distance of approximately 1.5 m beyond the edge of the foundations and sloped away from structures to provide drainage.

Hollow sections are allowed provided proper corrosion protection is considered
All bolts in elevated steelwork connections shall be minimum grade ASTM A325 or A490 high strength bolts to suit the required design. All holding down bolts shall be minimum grade ASTM A307. Finishes etc. shall be selected such, to eliminate galvanic corrosion. Bolt finishes shall conform with the finishes applied to the steelwork elements which they connect. Welded connections will comply with the AWS D1.1 of the American Welding Society.
Non Destructive Inspection shall fulfill the requirements of AWSD1.1 of the American Welding Society.
The Contractor shall select coating systems on consideration of climatic conditions prevailing at the site. Such systems shall have a design life to first maintenance of at least 25 years. The contractor's particular attention is drawn to the maritime environment and high levels of windblown salts prevailing at this site. This  shall  consist  of  shop  applied  coatings  and  site  applied  finishing  coat(s)  all  in  accordance  with BS EN ISO  12944.  The  final  site  coat(s)  shall  be  applied  after  steelwork  erection/alignment  and  bolt tightening activities have been completed, unless otherwise agreed with the Owner.
Fire protection to the structural steelworks/ steel structures which are exposed to lube oil fire, shall be intumescent paint system in exposed solutions, and fire-resistant board system or vermiculite or spray system in concealed areas to give 2 hour fire protection when tested in accordance with NFPA.
When required the paint shall be sprayed or applied in accordance with the manufacturer's approved methods onto previously primed structural steel. Suitable mesh 'reinforcement' shall be incorporated to prevent loss insulation when subject to physical damage.

The Contractor shall provide and install a lightning protection system to provide the necessary protection to  each  building.  Each  building  shall  have  its  own  air  terminal  network,  down  coming  tapes and earth points.
The Contractor shall connect together with a perimeter conductor all earth rods of each individual lightning system. From the nearest point of the perimeter conductor the Contractor shall provide a link to the Plant earthing system.
The building lighting protection system is to be executed to:
- -IEC 62305-1:2010
- -IEC 62305-3:2010 and
- -IEC 62305-4:2010
And alongside protection of human life, shall prevent damage not only to buildings, but also to electrical and electronic installations.

The domestic hot and  cold-water  services  within  the  buildings  shall  comply  with  the  requirements  of BS6700: 2009 -'Design, installation, testing and maintenance of services supplying water for domestic use within buildings and their curtilages'
When the direct potable water supply is not applicable, the Administration and Control Building, Social Building, Workshop and General Store and Gatehouse shall be provided with a cold-water storage tank of sufficient capacity to meet one day's consumption for the building or area served. The tanks shall be of GRP insulated construction, shall be located so as to prevent water damage or consequential losses in the event of a tank leakage for any reason and shall feature condensation drip trays to prevent nuisance damage. All tanks which are located above water sensitive areas should be surrounded by a bund wall with adequate evacuation ducts.
The hot water systems shall be served from local electrical water heaters, with central storage systems being provided only for large buildings with heavy demand for hot water.
The Contractor shall also include for Potable Water supplies to emergency wash-down and shower facilities in battery rooms and chemical areas, and to HVAC humidifiers.
The Contractor shall include for all necessary inspection, testing and commissioning, including disinfection, of the complete hot and cold-water services installations.

HVAC systems shall be designed, installed and commissioned in accordance with the latest applicable codes of the following:
- ASHRAE American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air Conditioning Engineers.
- SMACNA Sheet Metal and Air Conditioning Contractors National Association.
- NFPA National Fire Protection Association.
- ARI American Refrigeration Institute.
- ANSI American National Standards Institute.
- AABC Associated Air Balance Council.
All systems shall be designed and installed to provide acceptable environmental conditions for each area. The conditions of temperature, humidity, air movement and air filtration shall be controlled as required in the respective areas in summer and winter.
HVAC  systems  serving  critical  areas  such  as  Control  Rooms  shall  be  provided  with  duty/standby  air handling and mechanical cooling plant to ensure continuity of operation.
HVAC systems shall be arranged to shut down in the event of a fire alarm, with installation of the fire dampers for each individual room, seal supply and extract ducts as required for the application of clean agent fire suppression systems and start up smoke control pressurization systems. Provision shall be made in all plant areas for the venting and clearance of smoke and fumes in the event of fire, by means of roof vents or extract fans.
All systems and components shall be suitable for the design life of the Plant, and be designed for minimum life cycle cost and complexity, consistent with functionality, ease of maintenance and reliability.
For all general cases the HVAC  systems  the ambient design conditions shall be  as  ASHRAE recommendations to suite the site conditions. The HVAC systems shall be designed to obtain the internal conditions  and  system  redundancy  as  indicated  in  the  OTS.  Central  air-conditioning  systems  having humidity control may be provided with air handling units for fresh air supply. These units shall be provided with cooling coils and steam humidifiers to handle the full dehumidification/humidification load for the central  system,  with  dew  point  control.  Fresh  air-cooling  coils  shall  have  10 per  cent  margin  on  heat transfer  surface  to  cater  for  periods  of  abnormally  high  humidity.  Face  air  velocity  shall  not  exceed 2.0 m/sec.
Humidification shall be by electric powered steam generators with proportional control and steam lance injection.
The  sound  levels  in  plant  and  occupied  areas  shall  not  exceed  the  Appendix  C  of  the  EPC  contract performance  guaranties  and  the  noise  limits  for  HVAC  systems  should  be  in  line  with  latest  ASHRE guidelines.:
Sound attenuators shall be provided in duct systems, as required, to achieve the above sound levels.
All HVAC units and systems shall be provided with local control panels for local manual/automatic control. The operation status such as alarms, humidity, temperature, fault indication, status indication of each air conditioning system shall be indicated and available at the local control panel and any individual fault signal results in a group signal, which shall be transmitted to the central control room.

In addition, the following criteria shall be considered in the design of the HVAC system:
- (i) A general lighting level dissipation of 33 watts/m²
- (ii) Sensible and latent heat gains for occupancy should be allowed on the basis of one person per 10m².
- (iii) A minimum quantity of fresh air should be provided at the rate of 0.00125m³/s per m² of floor area or 12.5 l/s/person, whichever is the greater and this should be shown in the calculations. All equipment gains within each room should be allowed for in determining Plant capacities.
- (iv) Re-circulated air  should  be  filtered.  Air  from  areas  where  pungent  fumes  are  likely  to  be present should not be re-circulated.
Battery rooms should be air conditioned by self-contained air conditioning units. The design of the air conditioning system shall avoid recirculation of air back into the battery room. These units should be of the non recirculative type and sized to provide the internal conditions previously specified with a minimum of five air changes per hour. Duplicate extract fans should be provided, mounted at high level and positioned such that accumulations of hydrogen cannot occur. The fan units, ducts and dampers should be suitable for long life in the acidic environment.
The WTP chemical area should be provided with acid vapor preservation systems, otherwise these areas should be isolated as individual rooms with HVAC materials properly selected for acidic environment.

Ductwork shall be fabricated, installed and tested in accordance with the latest SMACNA Standards. General supply  and  extract  system  ductwork  shall  be  of  galvanized  sheet  steel  construction.  Irrespective  of pressure/velocity classification, ductwork at low level in plant rooms and in areas subject to mechanical damage shall be constructed (as a minimum) to medium pressure standard.
All duct systems shall be complete with dampers to facilitate balancing and fire dampers. Splitter dampers will not be accepted. Access doors shall be provided as required for inspection/maintenance of dampers, fire dampers, instruments etc. Final connections to ceiling-mounted supply and extract terminals may be carried out in insulated flexible ductwork.
Extract system ductwork from battery rooms and chemical areas shall be of PVC construction.
High-pressure ductwork shall be pressure/leak tested. Low and medium pressure ductwork need not be tested, except where located outdoors.
The following ductwork shall be insulated:
- Fresh air ductwork
- Low Temperature supply and extract ductwork.
- Medium temperature supply ductwork.
- Ductwork in Electrical rooms, where subject to condensation.
Fire dampers to UL Standards and NFPA-90A shall be provided on ductwork systems passing through firewalls and floors, and as required for compartmentation of gas fire suppression systems.
Dampers shall be operated by fusible link and (re-settable) damper motor, suitable for actuation through the fire detection system and fire damper control panel. Smoke dampers for clean agent fire suppression systems shall be motor operated/solenoid actuated for closing and opening purposes. Damper status shall be indicated on the control panel mounted adjacent to the Fire Control panel.

All fresh air intakes on large central systems shall be provided with inertial type sand filters, with access sections behind. Small systems employing fixed volumes of fresh air shall be provided with sand louvres.
Primary  and  fresh  air  filters  on  all  systems  shall  be  permanent  metal  panel  washable  type,  dust  spot efficiency 20 per cent. A complete set of spare cells shall be provided for cleaning, along with coating fluids. Washing facilities shall be provided, with service water being used for cleaning.
Secondary air filters on medium temperature systems serving plant areas shall be replaceable bag filters, dust spot efficiency 50 per cent. Secondary air filters on low temperature systems serving offices/control rooms/electronic areas shall be replaceable bag filters, dust spot efficiency 90 per cent.
All  bag  filters  shall  be  supported  in  proprietary  mounting  frames  for  front  or  side  withdrawal.  The Contractor shall supply a sufficient number of replacement cells to last during the test periods and during the Defects Liability Period, with one complete set being provided at that the end of the Defects Liability Period.

- o 1 No. Locker Room (50 lockers);
- o Toilet Rooms, Wash Basin, shower Room for Male and female.
- o Canteen.
- o Kitchen and Dining Hall.
- o One Designated smoking area (to be arranged outside the building);
- o One Social Room for the plant O&M staff.
- o Prayer room.
- o Shaded Car Park -50 parking area.
The final size shall be decided during detail engineering stage subject to Owner's approval.
The administration building shall be combined with Social building.
The  Contractor  shall  provide  all  necessary  expertise,  labour,  construction  plant  and  equipment,  and materials for the satisfactory construction of the Works.
On the basis of the approved design calculations and design drawings, the Contractor shall prepare all necessary  construction  drawings  and  design  works  associated  with  these  drawings  including,  but  not limited  to,  architectural  construction  and  detail  drawings,  building  services  construction  and  detail drawings, layout and placing drawings for reinforcing steel, reinforcing bar detailing and bar schedules/drawings,  concrete  placement  drawings,  formwork  and  shuttering  drawings,  design  of connections between structural steelwork members, preparation of detailed shop structural steelwork fabrication and erection drawings, material lists and weight schedules etc.
The scope of supply shall cover, in addition to any other necessary components which may be required for the proper and continuous commercial operation of the complete installation including any and all auxiliary systems, the complete construction of all components specified in this OTS (and including but not limited to all labour and material procurement, delivery, transport, supplementation, maintenance, consumables, dismantling of all auxiliary and ancillary work and furthermore, all insurance, handing over of all work in satisfactory condition,  maintaining during the guarantee period until the final acceptance of the entire complete works).
The Contractor's scope of work shall include all activities necessary to properly design, supply and execute all  works  for  the  facilities,  infrastructure,  substructures  and  superstructures  of  all  the  above  items,  as detailed in this OTS. Any works that are not specifically mentioned but are evidently needed for the proper supply and execution of the Work, shall also be included and shall be carried out in accordance with the relevant standards of this OTS.
The EPC shall repair all facilities Owned by other agencies, public and/or private facilities damaged through his use up to the satisfaction of the Owner.

The plant shall be provided with a process control system based on redundant configuration for safe and reliable operations with high availability. The design, control philosophy, redundancy concept, grade of integration, etc. will be subject to review, comment and approval by the Offtaker. The scope of supply shall include - but not be limited to - the following systems and components:
- Primary sensors, transmitters, actuators minimum equipment required shall be according to relevant IEC code or International Standards
- Plant control and monitoring system (DCS -Digital Control System) for CCR & Supervisory Control  and  Data  Acquisition  (SCADA)  for  the  Substation  and  other  Plant  packaged systems, including all necessary software licenses for the Plant with redundant operator stations and additional one operator / engineering station.
- The plant and control and monitoring system shall be designed to fulfill all Cyber Security regulations including HCIS requirements and international standards such as ISO 27000 series (especially ISO 27001,ISO 27002 and ISO 27019
- The network architecture shall be designed using quadrant segregation and will fulfill all requirements as per ACWA cyber security policy.
- Long-term  data  server  via  RAID  station  (Redundant  Arrays  of  Independent  Disks)  for central back management and archiving.
- Network with routers and switches
- Copper/FO-converters where applicable
- Plant monitoring system and performance calculation (at all design conditions).
- Settlement metering system including check meter shall be provided in line with the latest version of the Grid Code at the date of the Bid submittal.
- Hardware and software for Plant Accounting Settlement System (PASS)) including and other  requirements  (data  transmission,  Remote  control  from  LDC,  cybersecurity,  AMI integration) as defined by Offtaker.
- Internal communication systems (telephone, public address system, LAN/ WAN system)
- GPS-based clock systems
- All relevant BOP system like HVAC, Fire-fighting and Fire detection systems, CCTV and surveillance systems in accordance with the country local requirements i.e. HICS KSA .
- Ergonomic designed control room
- Field testing equipment
- Instrument workshop equipment.
